description: In this course students learn the basic building blocks of virtual instrumentation and the LabVIEW software on which a VI is implemented, how sensor signals are communicated to a computer and processed by algorithms built in LabVIEW, and how to design systems for solving engineering problems.

syllabus.title: Introduction to Virtual Instrumentation
syllabus.body: Brief history of the development of virtual instrumentation (VI) systems, block diagram of a VI, role of hardware and software in a VI, VI for test, industrial I/O and control and design, VI applications in the engineering process, difference between traditional instruments and the VI, data-flow techniques, graphical and textual programming, comparison with conventional programming.

syllabus.title: VI Programming Techniques
syllabus.body: Front panel and block diagram, controls, indicators and data types, functions and operations in the block diagram, sub-VIs, icon and connector pane, repetition and loops (for and while loops), case and sequence structures, structure tunnels, shift and stacked registers, feedback nodes, local and global variables, charts, arrays, matrices and clusters, polymorphism, waveform graphs and charts, formula nodes, string and file I/O.

syllabus.title: Data Acquisition Basics
syllabus.body: Analog, discrete and digital signals, resolution, registers and counters, analog to digital converters (R-2R ladder network, weighted resistor method), digital to analog converters (counter type, tracking type, dual slope, flash type, SAR), timing and interrupts, data acquisition systems - sensor module, signal conditioning, multiplexing, sample and hold circuit.

syllabus.title: Applications
syllabus.body: Case studies and applications of VI related to control systems, power electronics and power systems, development of a PID controller.

outcomes: Have knowledge of various functionalities of the LabVIEW software.
Build a VI for various applications.
